subject: Realtime stream stalls during high-throughput demo
messages:
From: Tara Singh <tara@brightleaf.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, BrightLeaf Support <ops+realtime@brightleaf.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Realtime stream stalls during high-throughput demo

Hi Michael / Redwood team,

We're seeing repeated stalls on the realtime streaming endpoint during today's demo traffic spike. The UI will start receiving tokens fine and then stop emitting for ~20-45s before a burst of tokens lands; sometimes the connection drops altogether with a 504/WS timeout. This happens when we push ~120 concurrent streams (each ~512 tokens/sec) from our demo harness.

We've attached a small pcap and a very short set of server-side traces (brightleaf-trace-20270228.tar.gz) showing the last two reproductions. Customer-facing demo is in ~90 minutes and we need a mitigation path.

Immediate ask: can you confirm this is a Redwood-side streaming issue vs our network? If you have any quick mitigations (switch model variant, route to a dedicated pool, or change keepalive/chunk flush), we can try them now.

Thanks,
Tara
Sr. Infra Eng, BrightLeaf

--
BrightLeaf Inc
ops+realtime@brightleaf.ai

Evelyn / Dylan — forwarding BrightLeaf's report. They hit a production demo spike and are getting streaming stalls and intermittent WS timeouts. Attachments from customer included (pcap + traces).

Summary:
- Impact: customer-facing demo; intermittent streaming silence for 20-45s, occasional 504/WS disconnects.
- Load: ~120 concurrent streams, each ~512 tok/sec (reported).
- Customer has provided pcap and a short trace bundle.

Immediate asks:
1) Can infra/edge confirm whether chunked-transfer buffering or idle timeouts on our fronting layer could explain the gaps?
2) If so, what's the fastest mitigation we can do today (config change, route to dedicated pool, enforce chunk flush every X ms, enable heartbeat frames)?

I put Tara on copy so we can coordinate a short test window. We're green to make short config changes.

-Michael

Thanks for flagging, Michael. This needs incident treatment — open INF-4218 and label P1.

Actions:
- Dylan: spin up a short war-room and prioritize triage. Check edge LB timeouts, nginx chunked flush policies, and any autoscale/backpressure behavior in the streaming router.
- Michael: give the customer a one-line acknowledgement and ETA (15–30 min) and propose fallbacks (route to dedicated pool or lower concurrency).
- I'll prepare an executive note if this becomes a wider customer impact.

For the near-term mitigation, prioritize: 1) enable aggressive chunk flushing (50–200ms) on the streaming edge, 2) ensure websocket ping/keepalive frames are passed through unchanged, 3) if we can route this customer's traffic to a dedicated pool in their region that should reduce shared-burst effects.

Evelyn
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tara Singh <tara@brightleaf.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Feb 2027 10:23:44 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Realtime stream stalls during high-throughput demo

Quick tech update from the war-room: attaching a short artifact set (edge-pcap-segment-20270228.pcap, realtime-ids-20270228.csv).

Observations so far:
- We see long gaps between chunk flushes at the HTTP edge; chunks are buffered for ~18–35s before a flush burst. That aligns with the customer-observed 20–45s silent windows.
- WS connections appear healthy (no TCP RST), but the proxy in front (nginx/our LB) is coalescing writes and under certain high-concurrency bursts it falls back to buffer-and-burst behavior.
- Error rate: during the spike we saw a ~2.6% increase in 502/504 on the realtime route and a token delivery latency tail shift (p99 increased from 220ms to ~2.4s).
- Throughput: overall token throughput is within expected limits, but per-connection fairness is impacted by the buffering pattern.

Immediate mitigations we've validated in a small test:
1) Toggle 'proxy_buffering off' and force chunked flush interval to 100ms on the streaming nginx fronting layer. This eliminated the 20–40s gap in our internal test.
2) If needed, we can temporarily route BrightLeaf's subdomain to a dedicated routing pool (requires a short DNS change/edge config) which eliminates multi-tenant burst interactions.
3) Add a lightweight application-level heartbeat token (single zero-length token) every 5s to keep client UX responsive while we fix buffering.

Requesting approval to apply (1) globally for the realtime route as an emergency config change and (2) to provision a dedicated pool for BrightLeaf for the demo window if they'd like — Michael, please confirm with the customer.

Dylan
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Tara Singh <tara@brightleaf.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Feb 2027 13:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Realtime stream stalls during high-throughput demo — proposed immediate plan

Tara — thanks for the data. We validated the root cause in a short war-room: our fronting proxy is coalescing chunked writes under bursty high-concurrency loads, which causes the silent windows you saw. Dylan pushed a small test change (proxy_buffering off + 100ms flush) that eliminated the gap in our test harness.

Proposed immediate plan for your demo window (option 1 or 2):
1) Fast path (recommended): We apply the streaming-edge config change now (proxy_buffering off; chunk-flush 100ms) and enable websocket keepalive passthrough. This is a low-risk config change and we've tested it internally. Expect ~10–15 minutes for validation and rollout.
2) Fallback: We provision a short-lived dedicated routing pool for your domain (30–90 minutes) which avoids multi-tenant burst interactions. This requires a DNS pointer update; we can do it in 20 minutes but it's slightly more operational overhead.

Which do you prefer? If you say "1", we'll proceed immediately and keep you posted every 5–10 minutes.

Attachments: brightleaf-trace-20270228.tar.gz (customer), edge-pcap-segment-20270228.pcap (SRE), realtime-ids-20270228.csv (SRE)

-Michael
